title: Exodus Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 6.

questions.question: What did the LORD say Pharaoh will do with a strong hand?
options: Let the Israelites go and drive them out of his land
questions.correctAnswer: Let the Israelites go and drive them out of his land
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:1 states that with a strong hand Pharaoh shall let the Israelites go and drive them out of his land.

questions.question: What name did God say He was known by to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: God Almighty
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:3 says God appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob by the name of God Almighty but was not known to them by the name Jehovah.

questions.question: What did God say He had established with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
options: A covenant to give them the land of Canaan
A new name for their descendants
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant to give them the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:4 states that God established His covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan.

questions.question: What did God say He had heard from the children of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Their groaning because of bondage
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:5 says God heard the groaning of the children of Israel whom the Egyptians kept in bondage.

questions.question: What did God promise to do for the children of Israel?
options: Bring them out from under the burdens of the Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them out from under the burdens of the Egyptians
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:6 promises God will bring the Israelites out from under the burdens of the Egyptians and redeem them.

questions.question: True or False: God said He will take the children of Israel to be His people and be their God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:7 says God will take the Israelites as His people and be to them a God.

questions.question: According to Exodus 6, what will God give the children of Israel as an heritage?
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:8 states that God will give the land of Canaan as an heritage to the children of Israel.

questions.question: Why did the children of Israel not listen to Moses when he spoke to them?
options: Because of anguish of spirit and cruel bondage
Because they did not know him
Because they were happy in Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Because of anguish of spirit and cruel bondage
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:9 explains that the Israelites did not listen to Moses due to anguish of spirit and cruel bondage.

questions.question: True or False: God instructed Moses to speak to Pharaoh and ask him to let the Israelites go.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:11 records God telling Moses to speak to Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of Egypt.

questions.question: What concern did Moses express before the LORD about speaking to Pharaoh?
options: He said he has uncircumcised lips and doubted Pharaoh would listen
He did not know the way
He wanted Aaron to speak instead
questions.correctAnswer: He said he has uncircumcised lips and doubted Pharaoh would listen
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:12 shows Moses telling the LORD he is of uncircumcised lips and questions how Pharaoh will listen to him.

questions.question: Who did God give a charge to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and Aaron
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:13 states that God spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt.

questions.question: In Exodus 6, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Speak to Pharaoh to let Israel go
Tell Israel the LORD will redeem them
questions.correctAnswer: Tell Israel the LORD will redeem them
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:6-7 instructs Moses to tell Israel that the LORD will redeem them before the other events occur.

questions.question: True or False: God said His name Jehovah was known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:3 states that God appeared to the patriarchs by the name God Almighty but was not known to them as Jehovah.

questions.question: What did God say He would use to redeem the Israelites from Egyptian bondage?
options: A stretched out arm and great judgments
questions.correctAnswer: A stretched out arm and great judgments
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:6 mentions that God will redeem the Israelites with a stretched out arm and with great judgments.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was the first to speak to the children of Israel after God spoke to him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:9 says Moses spoke to the children of Israel, though they did not listen due to their anguish and bondage.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Moses concerning Pharaoh, according to Exodus 6:11?
options: Speak unto Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of his land
Ask Pharaoh to make the Israelites slaves
Request Pharaoh to increase the Israelites' burdens
Tell Pharaoh to ignore the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Speak unto Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of his land
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:11 states that the LORD told Moses to speak to Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of his land. This command is foundational to the deliverance of Israel from Egypt, as reiterated in verses 13 and 27.

questions.question: How did Moses express his concern to the LORD about speaking to Pharaoh as described in Exodus 6:12?
options: He was worried because the children of Israel did not listen to him
He lacked confidence in his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: He was worried because the children of Israel did not listen to him
questions.explanation: In Exodus 6:12, Moses tells the LORD that the children of Israel have not hearkened unto him, and he questions how Pharaoh will listen to him since he is of uncircumcised lips. This shows his concern and humility before the task.

questions.question: What charge did the LORD give to Moses and Aaron as per Exodus 6:13?
options: To bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt
To build a temple for the LORD
To write down the laws for the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: To bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:13 records that the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt. This divine mission is central to the chapter and links to the command in verse 11 and the dialogue in verse 12.

questions.question: According to Exodus 6:14, who were the sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn?
questions.correctAnswer: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi
questions.explanation: Verse 14 lists the sons of Reuben as Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. This genealogical detail highlights the family heads and connects to the broader listing of tribes and families in verses 15-19.

questions.question: How does Exodus 6:15 describe the sons of Simeon?
options: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman
questions.correctAnswer: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:15 describes the sons of Simeon as Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman, emphasizing the family lineage and the inclusion of Shaul whose mother was a Canaanite, which may be significant in understanding family dynamics.

questions.question: According to Exodus 6:16, who were the sons of Levi and how long did Levi live?
options: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari; Levi lived 137 years
Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; Levi lived 120 years
Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel; Levi lived 130 years
Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul; Levi lived 140 years
questions.correctAnswer: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari; Levi lived 137 years
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:16 states that Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, and that Levi lived 137 years. These details provide the generational context for the Levites’ role, as further expanded in the following verses.

questions.question: What does Exodus 6:17 say about the sons of Gershon?
questions.correctAnswer: Libni and Shimi
questions.explanation: Verse 17 specifically names Libni and Shimi as the sons of Gershon, connecting to the families descended from Levi and showing the detailed genealogical structure important for Israel’s priestly heritage.

questions.question: What relationship between Amram and Jochebed is given in Exodus 6:20?
options: Amram took Jochebed, his father's sister, to wife
They were cousins from different tribes
questions.correctAnswer: Amram took Jochebed, his father's sister, to wife
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:20 explains that Amram married Jochebed, who was his father's sister, highlighting a close family marriage. This verse also mentions that she bore Aaron and Moses, key figures in Israel’s deliverance.

questions.question: What does the genealogy in Exodus 6 teach us about God's faithfulness in the context of His promises to Israel?
options: God preserves the lineage and fulfills His covenant through generations
God changes His promises over time
Genealogy is unimportant to God's plan
God only focuses on individuals, not families
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves the lineage and fulfills His covenant through generations
questions.explanation: The detailed genealogies in Exodus 6:14-20 emphasize God's faithfulness in preserving the family lines through which His covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are fulfilled, as introduced in verses 4-8.

questions.question: How does Moses' hesitation about his ability to speak relate to his mission, based on Exodus 6:12 and 6:30?
options: Moses feels inadequate because of his 'uncircumcised lips', doubting how Pharaoh will listen
Moses is confident and eager to speak to Pharaoh
Moses refuses to speak to Pharaoh
Moses believes Pharaoh will obey without speaking
questions.correctAnswer: Moses feels inadequate because of his 'uncircumcised lips', doubting how Pharaoh will listen
questions.explanation: Both Exodus 6:12 and 6:30 record Moses expressing his concern about his speech, calling himself of 'uncircumcised lips,' which metaphorically shows his sense of inadequacy for the mission to confront Pharaoh.

questions.question: What does Exodus 6:19 say about the sons of Merari?
questions.correctAnswer: Mahali and Mushi
questions.explanation: Verse 19 names Mahali and Mushi as the sons of Merari, completing the genealogical listing of Levi’s descendants and showing the organization within the tribe essential for their priestly duties.

questions.question: In the context of Exodus 6, what biblical virtue can a believer learn from Moses’ honest expression of his fears to God?
options: Humility and trust in God despite personal inadequacies
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and trust in God despite personal inadequacies
questions.explanation: Moses' honest confession of his 'uncircumcised lips' in Exodus 6:12 and 6:30 teaches humility and reliance on God’s strength, showing that even when we feel inadequate, trusting God leads to obedience and fulfillment of His purpose.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 6:13 indicates that both Moses and Aaron were given the charge to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:13 explicitly states that the LORD spoke unto Moses and Aaron and gave them the charge to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt, confirming both were commissioned together.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 6:20, Aaron and Moses were brothers born to Jochebed, who was Amram's sister-in-law.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:20 states that Amram took Jochebed, his father's sister, to wife and she bore Aaron and Moses. Jochebed was his aunt, not sister-in-law, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 6:15, Shaul, son of a Canaanitish woman, was one of the sons of Simeon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:15 lists Shaul, son of a Canaanitish woman, as one of the sons of Simeon, showing the inclusion of mixed lineage within the tribe's genealogy.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 6.

questions.question: Who did Aaron marry according to Exodus 6, and who were their children?
options: Elisheba, mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar
Miriam, mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar
Zipporah, mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar
Elisheba, mother of Moses and Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: Elisheba, mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:23 states that Aaron took Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, to wife, and she bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name 'Jehovah' as revealed in Exodus 6:3?
options: It was not known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
It means God Almighty and was known to the patriarchs
It refers to the God of the Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: It was not known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:3 says that God appeared to the patriarchs by the name God Almighty, but by the name Jehovah He was not known to them, indicating a revelation of a new aspect of God's identity.

questions.question: Which of the following sons belonged to the tribe of Izhar?
questions.correctAnswer: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:21 lists Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri as the sons of Izhar.

questions.question: According to Exodus 6, who was the father of Moses and Aaron?
questions.correctAnswer: Amram
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:20 states that Amram took Jochebed to wife and she bore him Aaron and Moses.

questions.question: Which family is identified as the 'families of the Korhites' in Exodus 6?
options: Sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph
Sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari
Sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi
Sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul
questions.correctAnswer: Sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:24 identifies Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph as the sons of Korah and the families of the Korhites.

questions.question: Who took one of the daughters of Putiel as a wife and had Phinehas as a son?
questions.correctAnswer: Eleazar, Aaron's son
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:25 states that Eleazar, Aaron's son, took one of the daughters of Putiel as a wife and she bore him Phinehas.

questions.question: What was Moses's concern when the LORD commanded him to speak to Pharaoh, according to Exodus 6:12 and 6:30?
options: That Pharaoh would not listen because Moses had uncircumcised lips
That he was not a skilled speaker
That Aaron would not support him
questions.correctAnswer: That Pharaoh would not listen because Moses had uncircumcised lips
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:12 and 6:30 show Moses expressing doubt that Pharaoh would listen to him because he says, 'I am of uncircumcised lips.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised to bring the children of Israel into the land He swore to give to their ancestors as an inheritance.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:8 states God will bring Israel into the land He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and give it as their heritage.

questions.question: Which of these statements about the sons of Levi is accurate according to Exodus 6?
options: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari were his sons
Amram was the son of Kohath
Phinehas was the son of Gershon
questions.correctAnswer: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari were his sons
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:16 states that Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the repeated affirmation 'I am the LORD' throughout Exodus 6, particularly in verses 2, 6, 7, 8, and 29?
options: Inclusio, framing the chapter to emphasize God's identity and promises
Chiasm, arranging ideas in an A-B-B-A pattern
Metaphor, comparing God to a shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the chapter to emphasize God's identity and promises
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase 'I am the LORD' at the beginning and end and throughout Exodus 6 forms an inclusio, framing the chapter around God's identity and covenant promises (Exodus 6:2,6,7,8,29).

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of God remembering His covenant and redeeming His people as found in Exodus 6:5-6?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 7:9
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 7:9 emphasizes God's faithfulness to His covenant and His lovingkindness to those who keep His commandments, echoing Exodus 6:5-6 where God remembers His covenant and promises redemption.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'redeem' in Exodus 6:6, and what does it signify in the context of Israel's deliverance?
options: Ga'al, meaning to redeem or buy back, signifying God's act of rescuing Israel
Shalom, meaning peace, signifying God's blessing
Chesed, meaning lovingkindness, signifying God's mercy
Ra'ah, meaning to see, signifying God's awareness
questions.correctAnswer: Ga'al, meaning to redeem or buy back, signifying God's act of rescuing Israel
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Ga'al' means to redeem or buy back and symbolizes God's powerful act of deliverance and rescue of Israel from Egyptian bondage as in Exodus 6:6.

questions.question: According to Exodus 6:26-27, what was the specific charge given by the LORD to Moses and Aaron?
options: To bring out the children of Israel from Egypt according to their armies
To offer sacrifices in the wilderness
To lead the children of Israel to Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: To bring out the children of Israel from Egypt according to their armies
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:26-27 states that the LORD charged Moses and Aaron to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt according to their armies.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri as recorded in Exodus 6.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:22 names Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri as the sons of Uzziel.

questions.question: Which cultural or historical context is reflected by Moses' concern about his 'uncircumcised lips' in Exodus 6:12 and 30?
options: A perceived inadequacy related to ritual purity and public speaking among Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: A perceived inadequacy related to ritual purity and public speaking among Egyptians
questions.explanation: Moses' phrase 'uncircumcised lips' likely reflects his awareness of ritual purity and cultural communication barriers, which would affect his acceptance before Pharaoh (Exodus 6:12,30), given the Egyptian context.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine name does God reveal to Moses in Exodus 6 to emphasize His eternal covenant faithfulness, which was not known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: JEHOVAH
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:3 reveals that God appeared to the patriarchs as 'God Almighty' but was not known to them by the name JEHOVAH, which emphasizes His self-existence and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Which theological doctrine is primarily taught in Exodus 6:4 regarding God's relationship with the patriarchs and the land of Canaan?
questions.correctAnswer: The covenantal promise of land
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:4 highlights God's established covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give them the land of Canaan, teaching the doctrine of the covenant promise regarding possession of the land.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated in Exodus 6:5 when He hears the groaning of the Israelites and remembers His covenant?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:5 shows God's mercy as He hears the suffering of His people and remembers His covenant, indicating His compassion and faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: How does Exodus 6:6-7 collectively teach the doctrine of salvation as it relates to God's deliverance of Israel?
options: God redeems with power and establishes a covenant people
Salvation is only through human effort
God's judgment is unrelated to salvation
Israel must earn deliverance by works
questions.correctAnswer: God redeems with power and establishes a covenant people
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:6-7 teaches that God will redeem Israel with a 'stretched out arm' (powerful salvation) and take them as His people, showing God’s sovereign grace in salvation and covenant relationship.

questions.question: In what way does Exodus 6:8 connect the promise of land with God's oath to the patriarchs, reinforcing His unchanging faithfulness?
options: God swears an oath to give land as heritage
The land is given only if Israel obeys
The land promise is conditional on sacrifices
The land promise is symbolic, not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God swears an oath to give land as heritage
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:8 states God will bring Israel into the land He swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, emphasizing His immutable faithfulness through an oath to fulfill the promise literally.

questions.question: What theological implication arises from the Israelites' refusal to listen to Moses as described in Exodus 6:9?
options: Human despair can hinder reception of divine promises
God’s promises depend on human acceptance
questions.correctAnswer: Human despair can hinder reception of divine promises
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:9 shows that the Israelites’ anguish and bondage caused them not to heed Moses, illustrating how human suffering and spiritual discouragement can block acceptance of God’s revelation.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'with a strong hand shall he let them go' in Exodus 6:1 reveal about God's method of deliverance?
options: God allows Israel to leave quietly
questions.correctAnswer: God uses powerful, sovereign intervention
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:1 indicates God’s deliverance will be accomplished by His sovereign power ('strong hand'), demonstrating His control over Pharaoh and history.

questions.question: How does Exodus 6:12 express Moses’ human limitation and what theological theme does this highlight?
options: Moses is confident in his speaking ability
questions.correctAnswer: Moses’ inadequacy emphasizes God’s grace
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:12 shows Moses’ concern about his 'uncircumcised lips,' highlighting human weakness and the need for God’s enabling grace in fulfilling divine missions.

questions.question: What role does Exodus 6:13 assign to Moses and Aaron in God's redemptive plan?
options: They are charged to bring Israel out of Egypt
They are to build the temple
They are to anoint the king of Israel
They are to write the law
questions.correctAnswer: They are charged to bring Israel out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:13 records that God gave Moses and Aaron the charge to bring the Israelites out of Egypt, making them key agents in redemption history.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by synthesizing Exodus 6:6 and Exodus 6:7 regarding God's redemptive work and covenant relationship?
options: God’s salvation leads to covenant people identity
Salvation is purely individual with no covenant
The covenant is conditional on Israel’s works
questions.correctAnswer: God’s salvation leads to covenant people identity
questions.explanation: Combined, Exodus 6:6 shows God’s deliverance and Exodus 6:7 reveals God’s intention to take Israel as His people, teaching that salvation results in covenant relationship.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s justice and judgment is taught in Exodus 6:6 when God promises to redeem Israel with 'great judgments'?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice accompanies His salvation
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:6 teaches that God's redemption involves executing just judgments on oppressors, showing that His salvation is inseparable from His righteous justice.

questions.question: How does Exodus 6:20 contribute to our understanding of the human lineage and divine preparation of Moses and Aaron?
options: It shows the family background and divine providence in their birth
It claims they were born in Egypt outside the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the family background and divine providence in their birth
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:20 details Amram and Jochebed as parents of Moses and Aaron, underscoring God's providential preparation of key redemptive figures within the covenant family.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's promises in the Old Testament are unreliable because of human disbelief. What does Exodus 6:9 teach about this scepticism?
options: Human unbelief does not negate God's promises
Promises depend on Israel's faithfulness alone
God changes His mind due to Israel’s doubt
Promises are symbolic and not meant to be fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: Human unbelief does not negate God's promises
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:9 shows Israel's disbelief and anguish despite God's promises, indicating that God's faithfulness is not contingent on human perception, affirming divine immutability (cf. 2 Timothy 2:13).

questions.question: What does the genealogical listing in Exodus 6:14-25 teach about the importance of lineage in God's redemptive plan?
options: God ordains specific families for priestly and leadership roles
Lineage is irrelevant in biblical theology
Only kingship lineage matters, not priestly
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains specific families for priestly and leadership roles
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:14-25 traces the Levite family lines, emphasizing God's sovereign choice of certain lineages (e.g., Aaron’s) for priesthood and leadership in salvation history.

questions.question: How does Exodus 6:29-30 reflect the ongoing tension between divine commissioning and human frailty in redemptive history?
options: Moses’ self-doubt contrasts with God’s command
God abandons Moses due to his weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Moses’ self-doubt contrasts with God’s command
questions.explanation: Exodus 6:29-30 shows God commanding Moses despite Moses’ admission of 'uncircumcised lips,' highlighting that God’s calling is not hindered by human weakness.
